    AI Overview
    The Artemis II crew successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, at 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT) on April 10, 2026. The crew concluded a 10-day mission around the moon and was recovered by a joint team aboard the USS John P. Murtha. 
    Key Details on the Artemis II Splashdown: 
    • Location: Pacific Ocean, near San Diego, California.
    • Time: 8:07 p.m. EDT / 5:07 p.m. PDT, April 10, 2026.
    • Spacecraft: Orion spacecraft ("Integrity").
    • Recovery Team: NASA and U.S. Navy personnel aboard the USS John P. Murtha. 
    This marked the end of the first crewed mission beyond low Earth orbit since 1972, with the crew (Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen) returning safely after a 10-day trip.
